To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polyclonal antibodies were produced against DNA modified with B[c]phenanthrenediol epoxide-2 and B[c]phenantherenediol epoxide-1.
polyclonal antibodies were raised against benzo[c]phenthrene diol epoxide modified DNA.
polyclonal antibodies were raised in New Zealand White rabbit against diastereomerc benzo[c]phenthrane-3,4 diol-1,2 epoxides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies to the detection of specific carcinogens and their adducts with DNA.
developing sensitive, specific and rapid methods to detect and quantify DNA damage caused by carcinogenic chemicals.
the development of antibodies to specific DNA adducts of polycyclic aromatic carcinogens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the polyclonal antibodies developed in this study were selective in their recognition of DNA modified with specific diastereomers of polycyclic aromatic diolepoxides.
the antibodies developed in this study have a high selectivity for B[c] PhDE-1-DNP and B[c] Ph DE-2-DNP.
polyclonal antibodies can be raised against DNA modified by a single polycyclic hydrocarbon diol epoxide and that they can be used to detect and quantitate that specific adduct in complex mixtures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed polyclonal antibodies to the diastereomeres of benzo[c] phenanthrene-3-4-diol- 1-2-epoxide.
the antisera developed against benzo[c]PhDE-modified DNA show high selectivity for DNA adducts of benzo[c] phenanthrene, but not for those formed by other polycyclic aromatic compounds.

we have developed a series of polyclonal antisera that are specific for DNA adducts formed by the major metabolites of benzo[c]phnenthrace, benzo[a]-pyrene, 7,12 dimethylbenz[a]-anthracene, and dibenz[a,h]anthracene.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polyclonal antibodies can be developed that have specificity for DNA modified by polycyclic aromatic diolepoxides.
we developed a polyclonal antibody that is specific for DNA adducts of benzo[c]phnathrene-3, 4-diol- 1,2-oxide.
polyclonal antibodies can be used to distinguish DNA adducts formed from different polycyclic hydrocarbons.
